newsitem.title: USA: Toro to realign irrigation plant operation.
newsitem.headline: Toro to realign irrigation plant operation.

text.p: Toro Co said Tuesday that administration and distribution functions at the Toro Hardie Irrigation facility in Laguna Niguel, Calif., will be moved to Toro's Riverside, Calif., irrigation headquarters.

The Laguna Niguel facility currently has 99 employees and all but 15 of those employees will be offered positions at Toro Riverside, it added. The move to Riverside will begin in mid-June and be completed by the end of November.
Toro also said it will exchange manufacturing expertise between Riverside and the Toro Hardie El Paso, Texas manufacturing plant.

All Toro irrigation valves will now be produced at El Paso, and all Toro irrigation spray production will now take place at Riverside. The shift is not expected to affect the number of jobs at each location.

"These moves reflect the continued integration of Hardie and Toro irrigation operations and will let each facility specialize in the production technology that they do best," Rick Perod, vice president and general manager of Toro's U.S. irrigation business, said in a statement.
Toro, which provides landscaping and irrigation products, acquired James Hardie Irrigation in December 1996.
